newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Curfew to be extended in crime-hit PNG.
newsitem.headline: Curfew to be extended in crime-hit PNG.

text.p: A two-month long curfew in Papua New Guinea is to be extended in the capital Port Moresby for a further two months, police commissioner Robert Nenta said on Tuesday.
He said extending the curfew, which runs from 10.00 p.m. to 5.00 a.m., would give police more time to tackle a wave of violent crime that has been sweeping the South Pacific nation.
Port Moresby is known as one of the world's most dangerous cities, with rising unemployment and urban drift leading to the growth of criminal gangs.
Police at the weekend shot dead a man suspected of taking part in one of two armed hold-ups, and arrested another six people.
Port Moresby police chief Philip Taku said earlier this week police were better prepared and equipped to fight crime, and warned criminals would not get away.
